side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 Distinct owners behind the composite; below 10 the cell is refused census_composite_below_k.

CC 2.6.1.2 lists scope with the optional members ("absent", "member absent"), unlike its rows for required members, which read "on one, admission refuses". CC 3.3.5 admits a consent_record with stance granted on three required fields, scope not among them. The family model's body for consent:state has no required scope. side_a: CC 5.3.3.6 "For accountable streams, "published" means **witness-cosigned** (the CC 5.3.1 path), so the subscriber cannot collude with the producer on a private root."
side_b: CC 8.10 "attest: `one transparency_log:cosigned:{tree_size}@admitted[val:log_id=leaf:stream_id,val:root_hash=val:chunk_root,leaf:tree_size>=val:K] else refuse` (CC 5.3.3.6)"
note: The card of delivery_receipt:{stream_id} refuses every receipt that has no cosigned head. The text asks for a published head, and makes 'published' mean witness-cosigned for accountable streams only; a best-effort stream publishes producer-signed roots alone (CC 5.3.3.3, witness cosign OPTIONAL). A receipt on a best-effort stream is admitted by the text and refused by the card, if transparency_log:cosigned is the witness-cosigned head as its name says.

side_a: CC 3.3.7: Pinning `self` is what forecloses a third party forging a grant in G's name, since only G signs with G's key as the attested-intent-holder.
side_b: CC 6.1.5.3: is the `cohorts` member of the owner's `consent:replication` grant for that node
note: CC 3.3.7 admits a replication grant only from the granting node's own key; CC 6.1.5.3 and CC 3.3.6.3 (any live roster key signs every owner act, consent included) make it the owner's grant for the node. The family model (code-v61) and the CC 8.10 card admit both: `replication: owner, self`. A node built to CC 3.3.7 alone refuses the owner-signed grant that sets the per-node allow list.

The manifest and the CC 8.10 card put it on `accord:lifecycle:{kind}`, the confirmation and the resumption, and the heartbeat's own card has no expiry. side_b: CC 4.4.3.2.8: "An affiliation that is not public carries a federation-scope listing row (`community:listing:v1`, [CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md)) naming those four things and nothing else."
note: What the public listing row is and holds. side_a: CC 4.5.13 Content survives **only** by an affirmative, on-record **keep-decision**
side_b: CC 4.5.13 When the live-majority vote **favors removal/moderation but the content is retained** (flagged, not hard-removed), it is **auto-hidden behind an active interstitial**.
note: The protective default gives two outcomes for a report raised in the room (removed unless a keep lands). The infohazard gate and the ladder give a third, "flagged-but-retained", when the majority favours removal, and nothing says when a vote for removal retains the bytes behind the interstitial and when it removes them. One reader destroys, the other keeps consent-gated.

side_a: CC 4.5.5 A's authority set ([CC 2.4.1.2.1](part_2_the_grammar.md)) plus any holder of a `review`-scoped chain from that set
side_b: CC 8.10 card reconsideration:{grounds}: attest: `one takedown_notice:{basis}@admitted[id=ref:*] else refuse` (CC 3.1.1)
note: The text lets a reconsideration target any prior action: a takedown, a moderation event, a licence, a slashing. The guard in transitions.json (reach whole, sourced from the CC 3.1.1 takedown row) refuses every reconsideration that does not name an admitted takedown_notice, so a contest of a licence or of a moderator's record is refused at the door. The text is the side the rest supports.

side_a: CC 4.3 Where the seat requires a licence the attester does not hold, it is refused `deferral_response_unlicensed`.
side_b: CC 8.10 card deferral:response:{outcome}: attest: `one licensure:{authority_id}@admitted[attested=signer] at asserted_at else refuse(deferral_response_unlicensed)` (CC 4.3)
note: In the text a licence is asked only where the seat row names a licensing authority ("A seat in a domain may require a licence"). The guard in manifests/transitions.json has no condition, so every deferral response from a signer with no licence is refused. The card also names the signers `steward, wa`; CC 4.3 admits the conferrer or any key on a live chain from it, an agent handed the answering included.

side_a: CC 3.1.3 the election id (digest of community id, roster head and last seating)
side_b: CC 4.5.13 Its id is the digest of the community id and of the last seating row or, for a room never yet seated, the genesis of the roster.
note: The ballot row of CC 3.1.3 puts the roster head into the election id. CC 4.5.13 leaves it out on purpose: "A member leaving while the room is locked therefore changes nothing about the election". With the head in the id a resignation during the lock makes a new id, and "a ballot naming an unknown election id ... is refused", so the ballots already cast fall under another election and two nodes seat differently.

side_a: CC 3.2: honest holders MUST delete past-epoch content keys, the epoch DEKs and `K_record_id` / `K_symbol`, after the window
side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.1: A member's new device at those scopes is granted every epoch that member's other devices already hold, by the minter's receive doors and sweep.
note: Under the default `rotate-forward` a holder deletes past-epoch community DEKs after 30 days; CC 4.4.3.4.1 and 4.4.3.4.5 (every grant held stays; nothing re-encrypted) have no such lapse and grant a new device every past epoch. Neither names the other; whether community history older than the window stays readable differs.

side_a: CC 2.6.6.3 such a community admits by invitation and the constraint describes it rather than gates it
side_b: CC 4.4.3.2.3 return false // location outside community's geographic bound
note: CC 2.6.6.3 (and the CC 3.2 district row) say a geographic community whose constraint is finer than resolution 7 admits by invitation and its constraint does not gate. evaluate_subkind_admission gates every geographic community on a contained, unexpired location_proof and has no finer-than-7 arm, so under it such a community can admit nobody at all. Part 2 and CC 3.2 support the invitation reading; the pseudo-code is the stale side.

side_a: CC 3.4.11 Admitted iff the signer acts for the subject (the subject's own occurrence or an admitted occurrence of it).

note: The model's signer cell, read from the shipped store, admits any registered key and records the text as silent; CC 3.4.11 and the CC 3.1.2 row ('not open-sender') admit only a signer acting for the subject. side_a: CC 3.4.9 **Single-source attestations** (only one of the two co-stewards has emitted) MUST be marked as `confidence ≤ 0.5` in consumer composition until the second co-steward's attestation arrives.

note: CC 3.4.9 caps a CIRIS-issued licence recorded by one of Registry or Verify at confidence 0.5; CC 4.4.3.8 honours a licence on two conditions (walk reaches the authority, charter declares the class) and names no second emitter. CC 2.4.1.2.1 and CC 4.4.3.8 (the homes) support the two-condition reading; the 0.5 rule has no counterpart there.

side_b: CC 3.3.1: which it emits for a lapsed grant (`expires_at`, or a `retain:<window>` in the scope) with `consent_supersedes` naming the grant
note: Two cells of one table name different members whose passing lapses a grant: valid_until (also CC 3.3.5, CC 4.4.3.5.5, reactions.json) against the row's expires_at or a retain window in the scope.
